topic: How does a deque (double-ended queue) work?
title: Deques: Both Ends Open

scenes.narration: A deque is a double ended queue. Think of a line where people may join or leave at either end. Ours starts with 4 at the front and 6 at the rear, and every operation touches one of the two ends.
scenes.caption: A line you can join at both ends

scenes.narration: First we push 9 onto the back, exactly like joining an ordinary queue. The deque now holds 4, 6 and 9, and the rear is 9.
scenes.caption: push_back(9)

scenes.narration: Now something a queue cannot do: we push 2 onto the front. The front is now 2, and the size is 4.
scenes.caption: push_front(2)

scenes.narration: Pop back removes the value at the rear, which is 9. That end behaves like the top of a stack, so the rear is now 6.
scenes.caption: pop_back()

scenes.narration: Pop front removes 2 from the front, just like dequeuing. The front is 4 again and the size is 2.
scenes.caption: pop_front()

scenes.narration: Finally we push 7 at the front. Every push and pop here took the same short time, because we only ever touch an end. The deque holds 7, 4 and 6.
scenes.caption: push_front(7)

scenes.narration: A deque gives you a stack and a queue in one structure. Use it for sliding windows, undo histories and any job that needs both ends.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: Push and pop at both the front and the rear
Every end operation takes O(1) time
One end acts like a stack, both ends like a queue

quiz.question: A deque holds 1 then 5. We push_front 3, push_back 8, then pop_front. What is at the front?
quiz.explanation: Pop front removes the 3 we just pushed, so 1 is at the front again.

quiz.question: A deque holds 2, 6 and 4. We pop_back, then push_front 9. What does it hold, front to rear?
quiz.explanation: Pop back removes 4, then 9 joins at the front.
